questions.question: What does fork() return in the parent vs child?
options: child pid in parent, 0 in child
0 in parent, child pid in child
questions.explanation: Parent learns the child's pid; child knows it is the copy via 0.

questions.question: What does exec() do to the calling process?
options: Replaces its memory with a new program, same pid

questions.question: Why call waitpid after fork?
options: To collect exit status and reap the zombie
questions.explanation: Dead children linger as zombies until waited on.

questions.question: Child calls exit() instead of _exit() after fork with buffered printf — risk?
questions.explanation: fork copies stdio buffers; exit flushes again. Use _exit in child.

questions.question: Copy-on-write means?
options: Copy all pages eagerly at fork
Share pages read-only until a write faults, then copy

questions.question: Where does WEXITSTATUS come from?
options: Kernel-saved exit code in PCB, read via wait
questions.explanation: Kernel stores it at exit; wait retrieves it.
